decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker-linked draft, as directly described by the Round 1 client: “The spec makes the title something I must enter.” Round 1 client rejects this: “I don't want to have to type the title myself every time” and requests saving “from just the address.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. Requiring a manually entered title diverged from the reference address-only saving flow; the client explicitly rejected that requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker-linked draft, as directly described by the Round 1 client: it “explicitly leaves automatic fetching out.” Round 1 client supplies the replacement behavior: paste an address and have the app fill in the page title, “ideally its description/icon,” automatically.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Automatic metadata collection was excluded, and the client supplied the reference-aligned behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “opening bookmarks”; Round 1 client says the presented saving/opening feature set “look[s] right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. The recorded decision to support revisiting the original link conforms at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “tags”; Round 1 client confirms that “tags … look right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bookmark organization through assigned tags is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “search”; Round 1 client confirms that “search … look[s] right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. The presented decision to provide bookmark search is conforming; the transcript does not present a contradictory search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes tags and “filters”; Round 1 client confirms that “tags … [and] filters … look right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. The presented tag/filter capability is reference-aligned.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “editing”; Round 1 client says “editing … look[s] right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. The recorded editing decision is conforming at the level presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “archiving”; Round 1 client confirms that “archiving … look[s] right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. Keeping bookmarks through an archive operation is reference-aligned.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “deletion”; Round 1 client explicitly approves “delete-with-confirmation.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bookmark deletion is conforming; confirmation is an additional safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “imports … are outside the initial release.” Round 1 client explicitly accepts the difference: “I'm fine leaving … imports … for later.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. Import was deferred despite being in the reference; the client explicitly identified and accepted that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “page archiving [is] outside the initial release.” Round 1 client explicitly accepts the difference: “I'm fine leaving … page archiving for later.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. Local preservation of bookmarked pages was deferred, and the client explicitly accepted the departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “the address-only saving flow” and says retrieval failures still save the bookmark. Round 2 client confirms: “I can now save a link just by pasting the address.”
decisions.note: Revised specification gate. The corrected URL-only saving decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker enumerates automatically retrieved metadata as title, description, and icon: “Page title is retrieved automatically” and “Description and icon are included when available,” without the required preview image. Round 2 client repeats only those fields and calls it “exactly what I wanted,” without identifying the missing preview image.
decisions.note: Revised specification gate. Metadata collection remained incomplete relative to REF-BM-02 because preview-image retrieval was not included; the response did not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Users can edit the title, and their edits won’t be overwritten.” Round 2 client confirms that the fetched title can be edited.
decisions.note: Revised specification gate. Editing auto-collected metadata after retrieval is reference-aligned at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents a plan covering address-only saving; Round 3 client verifies “saving a link from just its address.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate. Address-only saving remains conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents “guarded metadata retrieval” under the previously revised metadata scope, with no addition of preview-image retrieval. Round 3 client approves “the title and details fetched safely” without mentioning the missing preview image.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate. The plan carries forward the partial metadata scope from Round 2, and the remaining REF-BM-02 difference is not surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker selects “SQLite with full-text search”; Round 3 client confirms the plan covers “searching.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate. Full-text search is a conforming implementation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents the implementation plan; Round 3 client confirms it covers “filtering.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate. The presented filtering capability is reference-aligned.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client identifies “editing” among the behaviors covered by the maker's plan and approves proceeding.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate. The recorded editing decision is conforming at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client identifies “archiving” among the behaviors covered by the maker's plan and approves proceeding.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate. The archive capability is reference-aligned.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client confirms the maker's plan covers “delete-with-confirmation.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate. Deletion remains conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “address-only bookmark saving” in the MVP tasks. Round 4 client approves “saving from an address.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. Address-only saving is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns 17 tasks to “saving and revisiting bookmarks”; the client approves the breakdown.
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. Reopening/revisiting saved links is reference-aligned.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker includes “metadata retrieval” in the task scope inherited from the Round 2 title/description/icon specification, with no preview-image addition. Round 4 client approves “details fetched” without identifying the missing preview image.
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. The tasks retain the incomplete metadata-field decision, and the response does not surface it.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns tasks for “tags”; Round 4 client approves “tags.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. Tag organization is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns tasks for “search”; Round 4 client approves the search coverage.
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. Search is reference-aligned at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns tasks for tags and “filters”; Round 4 client approves the feature group.
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. Filtering is conforming at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns nine tasks covering “editing”; Round 4 client approves editing coverage.
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. Editing is reference-aligned at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns tasks for “archiving, restoration”; Round 4 client approves “archiving, restoring.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. Reversible archiving, distinct from deletion, conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns tasks for “deletion”; Round 4 client approves deleting.
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate. Deletion remains conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports automatic metadata fetching in the completed bookmark application; Round 5 client verifies that a link can be saved “just by pasting its address.”
decisions.note: Implementation review. The implemented address-only save flow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports completed “automatic metadata fetching” under the established title/description/icon scope, with no evidence that preview-image fetching was added. Round 5 client praises “the title and details gathered for me” but does not identify the missing preview image.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The implemented metadata behavior remains incomplete against REF-BM-02, and the response does not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports delivered “tags”; Round 5 client verifies that bookmarks can be organized with tags.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Tag assignment is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports delivered “search”; Round 5 client says search finds bookmarks again.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The presented search behavior is reference-aligned.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports delivered “filters”; Round 5 client verifies filtering to find bookmarks again.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The presented filtering behavior is reference-aligned.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports delivered “editing”; Round 5 client verifies that bookmarks can be edited.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Editing is conforming at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “archiving/restoring”; Round 5 client verifies both archive and restore operations.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Reversible archiving, distinct from deletion, conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “confirmed deletion”; Round 5 client verifies deletion with confirmation.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Permanent deletion capability is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker declares implementation complete without import, consistent with the Round 1 exclusion. Round 5 client explicitly states the expectation and accepts deferral: “it'd be nice to bring in my existing bookmarks from a file … No changes needed today.”
decisions.note: Implementation review. Import remains absent; the client explicitly identifies the desired capability and accepts the implemented departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker declares implementation complete without page snapshots, consistent with the Round 1 exclusion. Round 5 client explicitly states the expectation and accepts deferral: “it'd be nice … to save whole pages for offline reading. No changes needed today.”
decisions.note: Implementation review. Local page preservation remains absent; the client explicitly identifies and accepts that departure.
